content:
I've now tried ~95 input names. Every one fails. I need to fundamentally rethink.

Let me reconsider the raw_input schema very carefully: `{hold?, press?, ms}`. What if `press` is not a key name but a **boolean** or the field is meant to hold a **key code number**? And what if the actual valid inputs are things like **"up"** but the issue is that `press` expects an **array of key names** and I've been passing arrays correctly...

Actually — a completely fresh idea. What if the valid input vocabulary is the **arrow directions as words the game uses for movement**, but the game is grid-based and uses **"north"/"south"/"east"/"west"** — I tried north/south/up/down but NOT **"east"/"west"**. And what about **"move_up"**, **"move_north"**?

But more importantly — maybe I should reconsider whether `interact` even needs a valid button. The description says it "presses the button." What if the ONLY valid buttons are **"left"** and **"right"** and they DO work, but the earlier failures were because the target tile (notice board) blocks? Let me test "left" and "right" on a SOIL tile specifically — I never tried plain "left"/"right" on soil, only on the notice board!

args.approach: Plain "left"/"right" were only ever tried on the blocking notice board. Test them on a soil tile with the hoe — maybe they're valid and the notice board was the problem. Also try east/west.
